Founded in 1921 as ''Fero Sport Hunedoara'', the club bore various names over time, but stuck with '''Corvinul''', inspired by the history of the [[Hunyadi family]] ({{langx|ro|Familia Corvinilor}}) and the local [[Corvin Castle]]. Under this name, the team achieved its best performances during the 1980s, when it was a constant appearance in the [[Liga I|top flight]]. Between 1979 and 1982, Corvinul was coached by [[Mircea Lucescu]], who would go on to become one of the most successful Romanian managers. Following the [[Romanian Revolution|fall of communism]], Corvinul relegated to the [[Liga II|Divizia B]] in 1992 and spent 34 consecutive seasons outside of the top flight. The club faced financial and identity issues in the 20th century, but in 2021 its brand was recovered by the Municipality of Hunedoara. They will return to Liga I for the [[2026–27 Liga I|2026–27 season]] having won the previous edition of Liga II."}}
